title: Elevance Health — CEO/Director Cluster Buy Into 10% Selloff After Strong Q2
summary: CEO Boudreaux (+$1.0M) and Director Peru (+$366K) bought ELV on 2026-07-17 — the day after a Q2 beat that raised full-year guidance to $27+ EPS — into a 10% one-week selloff driven by peer-group Medicare Advantage fears. Setup pays if the sector's margin-cycle bottom is in.
catalyst: Elevance reported Q2 2026 on 2026-07-15: adj. EPS $7.45, operating revenue $49.8B, and management raised 2026 guidance to at least $27/share (from ≥$26 modeling floor) while affirming Medicare Advantage on track for ≥2% operating margin. Stock then fell 10.4% over the following week on unrelated peer noise. Two days later CEO Gail Boudreaux (2,725 sh @ $367.79 = $1.00M) and Director Ramiro Peru (1,000 sh @ $366.05 = $366K) filed Form 4 open-market buys — the first CEO buy of size in years[1][2][3].
thesis: Managed-care sentiment has been dominated by UNH-driven margin fears, dragging the whole peer group down. But Elevance's Q2 print told a different operational story: MA margin on plan, Medicaid identified as trough-year (management explicitly guided ≥12% adj. EPS growth in 2027 off the higher 2026 base), and $6B+ operating cash flow. When the CEO writes a personal $1M check the day after telling the market things are fine, they are signaling the sector-wide multiple compression has overshot company-specific fundamentals. The catalyst is falsifiable: two consecutive quarterly prints where Medicare Advantage MLR trends and Medicaid margin re-rate confirm the trough call[4].
counter_thesis: The bear case: Medicare Advantage utilization pressure is not company-specific but a structural industry step-change (higher acuity in the retained MA cohort as risk-adjustment methodology tightens under CMS v28 phase-in). Peer weakness (UNH, HUM, CVS) may reflect a real, persistent margin reset that ELV can defer for one quarter but not avoid. Medicaid re-determination tail risk continues into 2027. Insider buys of ~$1.4M combined against a $80B+ market cap are small in relative terms; CEO buying can be optical / compensation-planning driven. Multiple compression from ~13x to ~9x forward has already priced 'MLR pain persists' — but if 2027 EPS growth misses the 12% bar, the stock could re-rate lower on downgrades.

ticker_rationale.ELV: #2 US managed-care insurer by revenue ($175B+ TTM). Q2 2026 beat raised full-year EPS guidance and affirmed ≥2% Medicare Advantage operating margin — a differentiated print vs peers. Forward P/E ~11x (screener 10.9x) is a ~30% discount to the 5-year median; historical entry point when insider cluster + earnings beat align has resolved higher within 12 months in the last two managed-care cycles (2018, 2023).

trade_construction.target_12mo: ELV $450 (+23% from $367); consensus targets: Bernstein $482, Guggenheim $455, RBC $424
trade_construction.stop_loss: ELV $312 (-15% from $367); would breach if Q3 print signals MA margin missing 2% target
trade_construction.position_size_pct: 1.5% initial; scale to 2.0% if Q3 print confirms MA trajectory

catalyst_calendar.event: Q3 2026 earnings — first confirmation of Medicare Advantage margin trajectory post-cluster-buy
Q4 2026 earnings — full-year MA margin print vs ≥2% commitment; 2027 EPS guide
CMS 2027 Medicare Advantage rate notice / risk-adjustment phase-in updates

risks: CMS v28 risk-adjustment phase-in accelerates 2027 MA margin pressure beyond ELV's guidance envelope
Medicaid rate negotiations in H2 2026 come in below ELV's -1.75% margin floor
Peer downgrades (UNH, HUM) continue to compress the entire managed-care multiple regardless of ELV-specific fundamentals
PBM/Rx cost trend re-accelerates on GLP-1 utilization spillover into specialty pharmacy

invalidation.trigger: ELV Q3 2026 Medicare Advantage operating margin prints below 1.5% (guidance floor breach)
Management withdraws or reduces 2026 EPS guidance below $26
Any additional peer-wide MLR shock that ELV explicitly guides to for its own book
